steps.title: Where would you look for this action?
steps.line: P6’s first give-up: Change the icon size.
steps.caption: The task was “Change the icon size”. This schematic locates the command in the menu; it is not a screenshot of Files. The report calls the icon-size controls “very hard to notice”. The command’s presence in the menu did not ensure that participants found it.

steps.title: Did everyone have the same difficulty?
steps.line: One task, all six participants: Change the icon size.
steps.caption: Difficulty labels describe completed tasks. “Could not complete” records an unfinished task; “Outside study scope” records an excluded approach. These are six first-time GNOME users in the Files 47 study, not a population failure rate or a timing measurement.
steps.picture: P1. Moderate. difficulty. P2. Could not. complete. P3. No. difficulty. P4. Very little. difficulty. P5. Moderate. difficulty. P6. Could not. complete.

steps.title: Six first-time users, eleven tasks, one colour each
steps.line: The report’s colours become scores: green 5 down to black 1.
steps.caption: Researchers for GNOME’s design team watched six people who had never used GNOME, aged 21 to 47, try eleven tasks in test builds of Files 47. Their report colours each attempt from green, no difficulty, to black, unable to complete. To plot attempts as journeys, this page scores green 5 down to black 1.
steps.picture: The report’s colour key with this page’s scores: green, 5, completed without any difficulty; yellow, 4, completed with very little difficulty; orange, 3, completed with moderate difficulty; red, 2, completed with severe difficulty; black, 1, unable to complete the task; gray, no score, approach outside the scope of the study; 1 label.
